enquiry: We run a cell culture process in an aqueous medium. Glucose and lactate are measured from samples, and the delay makes it difficult to see changes promptly. We are exploring an in situ spectroscopy pilot that can be checked against those existing laboratory measurements. The medium and cell population change during the run; we have not yet selected a probe or a calibration strategy.

steps.step: Collect representative broth samples across the expected variation: early/mid/late phase, different cell densities and medium states.
steps.purpose: Cover the chemical and physical variation the calibration must span.

steps.step: Measure each sample with the Raman probe (M1) and, if the broth is clear enough, the NIR transmission/transflection probe (M2) under controlled conditions.
steps.purpose: Test the single methods first before any combination.

steps.step: Obtain independent laboratory glucose and lactate reference values for every sample, taken close in time to the spectral measurement.
steps.purpose: Provide the calibration and validation targets.

steps.step: Build one chemometric model per method and validate on held-out runs or batches, comparing predicted vs. reference values.
steps.purpose: Quantify each single method's accuracy honestly.

citations.quote: Chemometric algorithms are implemented in specialized software that enables preliminary data preparation (preprocessing), construction, validation, and application of predictive models

steps.step: Only if no single method meets the customer's accuracy target, test the Raman + NIR fusion against the best single method on the same held-out runs.
steps.purpose: Go/no-go: the fused model must beat the best single method, otherwise drop the extra instrument.

feasibility_plan.reference_measurements: Existing laboratory glucose and lactate measurements, with method and accuracy confirmed (Q4).
feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Customer-defined accuracy and update-interval targets (Q2) applied to held-out validation runs; go if the pilot meets them, no-go or method change otherwise.

assumptions: The broth is a liquid that can be accessed by an immersion probe at a suitable port.
The existing laboratory measurements can serve as the reference method for calibration and validation.
Concentrations of glucose and lactate are within ranges detectable by at least one of the shortlisted methods; this is checked by Q1.

solution_options.maintenance: Moderate; two optical windows and two instruments

solution_options.ease_of_use: Two instruments and probes running simultaneously
solution_options.maintenance: Higher; each block needs its own calibration and diagnostics

solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion of synchronised Raman and NIR spectra into one augmented matrix, as in the published pharma example. Both probes must sample the same well-mixed spot and the data must be normalised to a common time step, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs or it is dropped.

citations.quote: Data processing for pharmaceutical tasks relies on "low-level data fusion," where the synchronized NIR and Raman spectra are merged into a single augmented matrix.
Ultimately, the measurement data must be normalized to a common time step.

assessment.chemometrics_note: Quantitative glucose and lactate prediction will need PLS-type calibration models built on the laboratory reference values, validated on held-out runs; the sources note NIR and Raman bands overlap or are weak, making chemometrics a necessary component.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The pilot's purpose is time-resolved in-line tracking of glucose and lactate to remove the sampling delay; acquisition rate and synchronisation with reference sampling times should be fixed in the trial design.
assessment.future_direction: If the pilot succeeds, a simplified multi-wavelength sensor approach (as shown for other applications in the sources) could later replace full-spectrum instruments for routine control.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If Q1/Q3 show the broth is highly turbid throughout, the NIR transmission branch of O2 would be replaced by a reflection or ATR geometry; if Raman alone meets the Q2 accuracy target, O1 suffices and no fusion is needed.
proposal.next_step: Run the multi-method lab trial on representative broth samples with paired laboratory glucose and lactate references, per the feasibility plan.

solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion of synchronised Raman and NIR spectra into one augmented matrix, as in the published pharma example. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs or it is dropped.

assessment.brief_answer: Test Raman first: it tolerates water and is shown detecting glucose and lactate directly in bioreactors. Open: concentration ranges, required accuracy, broth turbidity and installation constraints decide the final probe and whether a Raman+NIR fusion is worth testing.

items.finding: The temperature sensitivity of the OH bands presents a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR.
items.how_it_applies: The assessment should consider whether temperature fluctuations in the culture medium could interfere with NIR measurements, potentially requiring strict temperature control or compensation.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This finding addresses aqueous solutions in general rather than this specific cell culture matrix or instrument setup.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data into a new matrix where variables from different sources are placed one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This approach can be tested to combine Raman and NIR spectral data for the cell culture monitoring pilot, provided the data streams are properly aligned.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited review discusses general analytical techniques rather than the specific combination of Raman and NIR in a cell culture bioreactor.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
